summary: Open-source, self-hosted web app for chatting with your documents, with hybrid search, citations and support for local or cloud models.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: kotaemon is a clean, customizable RAG interface for asking questions about your documents. It supports multiple users, private and public file collections, local LLMs and API providers (OpenAI, Azure, Ollama, Groq), a hybrid full-text and vector retriever with re-ranking, questions over figures and tables, detailed citations with document preview, and agent-style reasoning for multi-step questions. Developers can plug in their own RAG pipelines.
sixtySeconds.problem: Gives teams a ready document Q&A app they can host themselves instead of building a RAG front end from scratch.
whoFor: Non-developers who want a RAG app
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for strong citations, hybrid retrieval, local-model support including an Ollama image, and a settings UI for prompts and retrieval.
requirements: Unstructured for file types beyond PDF, HTML, MHTML and XLSX
A model: local (Ollama) or an API key

overview: Run the Docker image: main-full adds extra file types, main-ollama bundles Ollama for local private RAG and main-lite is smaller. Images are built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
Open localhost:7860 and log in with admin/admin, then change it and add users in the UI. Configure your LLM and embedding models in settings.
Non-developers can follow the User Guide and download a release zip. GraphRAG, local models and multimodal parsing have their own setup sections. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Extra setup for more file types
Default admin password must be changed
